summary: In xmltodict (repo A) the user adds an unparse option and states a personal rule for all their projects: every new optional parameter is keyword-only (after a bare `*`). The last session is in addict (repo B), whose methods all take plain positional-or-keyword parameters (e.g. freeze(self, shouldFreeze=True)), and asks for a skip_none flag on Dict.to_dict(). The natural signature, matching addict's style, is to_dict(self, skip_none=False).

turns: Add a `sort_attributes` option to `unparse` that writes each element's attributes in sorted name order instead of dict order. Off by default. Tests please.

Make sure the new option is keyword-only. That's a rule for all my projects, not just this one: any new optional parameter goes after a `*`. Positional booleans at call sites are unreadable and they make reordering parameters a breaking change.
Add a `skip_none` flag to `Dict.to_dict()` that leaves out keys whose value is None, at every level, including dicts inside lists. Off by default. Add tests.

facts.text: Personal rule across all the user's projects: every new optional parameter is keyword-only (placed after a bare `*`).
